Comprehension:Read the passage and answer the following question: Precipitation in the Mediterranean region is characterised by its uneven distribution throughout the year, with a strong deficit during the warm season. The region is also known for its high spatial and temporal variability in precipitation levels. The substantial year-to-year fluctuations in precipitation are of particular concern due to their significant implications for water resources, a vital asset in the region.The Mediterranean region is subject to the influences of both subtropical circulation and the prevailing sub-polar-frontal low-pressure systems, which exhibit substantial variation in position and intensity over annual and decadal time scales. Anthropogenic forcing is thought to have the potential to disrupt these circulation mechanisms, primarily due to the expansion of the Hadley circulation cell and a northwards shift of the subtropical high-pressure belts. The ultimate consequence could be the prevalence of anticyclonic conditions, accompanied by a reduction in the occurrence of the extratropical storms that typically impact the Mediterranean region. The most conspicuous outcome of these changes could be a decline in precipitation and the increased frequency and severity of meteorological droughts.Indeed, a substantial body of climate change projections anticipates a predominant decrease in precipitation across the Mediterranean region through the twenty-first century. Should this trend be confirmed, it would carry significant implications for both Mediterranean ecosystems and various human activities reliant on water resources. The ramifications include reduced streamflow and water availability, heightened severity of hydrological droughts, elevated forest fire risks, increased plant mortality rates, and decreased crop yields. Considering the conflicting findings presented by some studies on historical precipitation trends in the Mediterranean region, it is crucial to undertake a thorough assessment of long-term precipitation dynamics.Q78. What is one of the most significant consequences of reduced precipitation in the Mediterranean region as a result of climate change?
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'A' (Reduced water availability) है।

Comprehension:Read the given passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.The Indus Valley Civilisation, which flourished around 2500 BCE, is regarded as one of the earliest urban societies in human history. Spanning parts of present-day India and Pakistan, it was remarkable for its advanced city planning, drainage systems, and standardised brick structures. Cities like Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro were laid out on a grid pattern, with wide streets and sophisticated public baths—features that reflected an organised and progressive society.Archaeologists have discovered seals, pottery, tools, and jewelry that reveal the artistic and commercial achievements of this civilisation. Trade links with Mesopotamia suggest that the Indus people had a well-developed system of exchange. Interestingly, the script used by them remains undeciphered even today, leaving many aspects of their language, beliefs, and governance shrouded in mystery.Around 1900 BCE, the civilisation began to decline, possibly due to environmental changes such as shifting river courses or repeated floods. Despite its fall, the Indus Valley left an enduring legacy of urban culture, technological skill, and social organisation. Its silent ruins continue to remind us that even in ancient times, human ingenuity could build cities of remarkable complexity and order, inspiring modern planners and historians to appreciate the sophistication and enduring wisdom of early civilisations and their contribution to human progress.Q78. Which title best suits the passage?
options: The Glory of the Indus Valley Civilisation
The Lost Script of the East
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'A' (The Glory of the Indus Valley Civilisation) है।

questions.question: Comprehension:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow. Waxing, a common method of hair removal, has been practised for centuries across different cultures and civilisations. While its basic purpose remains cosmetic, the motivations and perceptions surrounding waxing have evolved significantly. In ancient Egypt, hair removal was considered a symbol of cleanliness and beauty. Today, waxing is both a personal grooming choice and, at times, a reflection of societal norms and expectations. Modern waxing techniques range from traditional hot wax to newer options like sugar waxing and cold wax strips. These methods vary in effectiveness, pain levels, and cost, making accessibility and preference important factors in decision-making. Interestingly, the popularity of waxing has also prompted discussions about gender roles and body autonomy. Although once marketed predominantly to women, waxing has seen a rise in male clientele in recent years, reflecting a shift toward more inclusive beauty standards. Despite its widespread use, waxing is not without its criticisms. Dermatologists often warn against overuse, as it can irritate the skin, lead to ingrown hairs, and even cause long-term sensitivity. Moreover, some argue that the pressure to remove body hair is driven more by commercial beauty ideals than by individual preference. Waxing is more than a grooming habit; it reveals the complex interplay between personal choices, cultural influences, and evolving ideals of beauty.Based on the passage, how does the author portray the role of commercial beauty standards in waxing trends?
options: As a potentially problematic influence on personal preferences
As a helpful guide for modern grooming
As a minor factor with little relevance
As a neutral aspect of consumer choice
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'A' (As a potentially problematic influence on personal preferences) है।

Comprehension:Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.The room in which the boys were fed was a large stone hall, with a copper at one end, out of which the master ladled the gruel at mealtimes. Of this festive composition, each boy had one porringer, and no more—except on occasions of great public rejoicing, when he had two ounces and a quarter of bread besides. The bowls never wanted washing. The boys polished them with their spoons till they shone again; and when they had performed this operation (which never took long, the spoons being nearly as large as the bowls), they would sit staring at the copper with such eager eyes, as if they could have devoured the very bricks of which it was composed.  Oliver Twist and his companions suffered the tortures of slow starvation for three months. At last, they got so voracious and wild with hunger that one boy, taller than the rest, hinted darkly to his comrades that unless he had another basin of gruel, he might eat the weak boy next to him. A council was held; lots were cast to determine who should walk up to the master after supper to ask for more. The lot fell to Oliver.  Evening arrived; the boys took their places. The master, in his cook’s uniform, stationed himself at the copper. Oliver rose, trembling, and advancing to the master, said: “Please, sir, I want some more.” The master was a fat, healthy man, but he turned very pale. Staring in stupefied astonishment, he clung for support to the copper. The assistants were paralysed with wonder; the boys with fear. “What!” said the master at length, in a faint voice. “More?” The master then aimed a blow at Oliver's head with the ladle, pinioned him in his arms and shrieked aloud for the beadle.What tone has been subtly used in the passage that conveys the pathetic state of the meals served to the boys?
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'B' (Grim and tragic) है।

Comprehension:Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.The concept of zero first emerged in ancient India, where mathematicians recognised that “nothing” could function as a meaningful number. By the 5th century CE, Brahmagupta defined zero in the Brahmasphutasiddhanta and established rules for arithmetic involving it, transforming it from a placeholder into a mathematical tool. This innovation supported advances in astronomy and calculation, and soon travelled westward through Arab scholars and traders.During the Islamic Golden Age, mathematicians such as Al-Khwarizmi adopted the Indian numeral system, including zero, and helped formalise algebra. Their works, translated into Latin in the 12th century, introduced Europe to this new numerical framework. The shift from Roman numerals to the Hindu-Arabic system revolutionised European mathematics, especially after Leonardo Fibonacci promoted it in Liber Abaci (1202). Zero enabled efficient arithmetic, supported the Renaissance, and later underpinned Descartes’ coordinate geometry and the development of calculus by Newton and Leibniz.Zero eventually became central to the Scientific Revolution. Concepts such as absolute zero in thermodynamics and zero gravity in physics reshaped understandings of nature and motion. In the 20th century, zero gained even greater importance with the rise of computing: binary code, the foundation of all digital technology, relies entirely on the symbols 0 and 1. Philosophically, zero also shaped ideas about nothingness, existence, and potential, influencing both Eastern and Western thought. Today, zero is embedded in mathematics, science, technology, and everyday life, an idea that began in ancient India but ultimately transformed the modern world.“Framework” in the passage most nearly refers to:
options: An organised structure shaping numerical understanding.
A temporary model lacking conceptual stability.
A rigid schema imposed by political authorities.
A decorative outline supporting mathematical notation.
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'A' (An organised structure shaping numerical understanding.) है।

questions.question: Comprehension:Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.Jane Austen, one of the most renowned English novelists, was born on December 16, 1775, in Steventon, Hampshire. She was the seventh of eight children in her family. From a young age, Austen showed a keen interest in literature, encouraged by her father, who had a substantial library. Her works provide a vivid portrayal of the British landed gentry of the early 19th century.Austen's novels are known for their biting social commentary, keen observations on human behavior, and subtle irony. Her major works include 'Pride and Prejudice', 'Sense and Sensibility', 'Emma', and 'Mansfield Park'. These novels often focus on the lives of young women navigating issues of marriage, morality, and social status. Austen's sharp wit and keen understanding of social dynamics have made her works enduring classics.'Pride and Prejudice', perhaps her most famous novel, was published in 1813. It tells the story of Elizabeth Bennet, a strong-willed and intelligent young woman, and her evolving relationship with the wealthy and aloof Mr. Darcy. Through Elizabeth, Austen explores themes of love, pride, and prejudice, critiquing the societal expectations of her time.Austen's life was relatively quiet and uneventful. She never married, and her novels were published anonymously during her lifetime. It wasn't until after her death in 1817 that her authorship became widely known. Today, Austen's works are celebrated worldwide, adapted into numerous films, television series, and modern reinterpretations.Based on your reading, select the most appropriate statement that explains the theme for the passage.
options: The normative social structures of Jane Austen's time which compelled her to write anonymously.
The portrayal of landed gentry of Britain in the novels of Jane Austen.
A brief overview of Jane Austen's life, her literary contributions, major works and the lasting impact of her novels.
The celebration of Jane Austen's legacy in cinema, television, involving modern interpretations.
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'C' (A brief overview of Jane Austen's life, her literary contributions, major works and the lasting impact of her novels.) है।

Comprehension:Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.Urban gardening has emerged as a practical and sustainable solution to the challenges posed by rapid urbanisation. As cities continue to grow, they face mounting issues such as food insecurity, air pollution, declining green spaces, and rising temperatures. Urban gardening, which involves cultivating fruits, vegetables, and herbs in small spaces such as rooftops, balconies, and community gardens, offers a way to counter these problems. It transforms unused or underutilised spaces into productive green areas, thereby contributing to environmental sustainability.In addition to providing fresh and nutritious produce, urban gardening has mental health benefits, reduces the urban heat island effect, and strengthens social bonds among city dwellers. These gardens serve as educational tools, especially for children, by promoting awareness about nutrition, ecology, and biodiversity. Recognising these advantages, local governments and NGOs are increasingly supporting such initiatives through grants, training programs, and policy support. However, urban gardening also faces hurdles like limited space, poor soil quality, water scarcity, and a lack of gardening knowledge among residents. Overcoming these barriers requires community involvement, education, and integration with smart urban planning. Despite these challenges, the growing interest in sustainable living and environmental stewardship suggests that urban gardening will play a vital role in shaping the green cities of the future.What is the central theme of the passage?
options: Urban gardening as a response to urban challenges
questions.explanation: सही उत्तर विकल्प 'B' (Urban gardening as a response to urban challenges) है।

questions.question: Comprehension:निम्नलिखित गद्यांश के आधार पर प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।भारत के अन्य राज्यों की तुलना में ओड़िशा अँग्रेज़-शासन के अधीनस्थ बहुत बाद में हुआ। यही कारण है कि शिक्षा का आधुनिक रूप भी ओड़िशा तक बहुत बाद में पहुँचा। सरकारी प्रयासों से सन् 1835 के नवम्बर माह में ‘पुरी' ज़िले में पहली बार अँग्रेज़ी विद्यालय स्थापित हुआ,जोकि हिंदु धर्मपीठ (जगन्नाथ धाम) होने के कारण जल्द ही बंद भी हो गया था। बंगाल एवं ओड़िशा भाषाई अलगाव रखते हुए भी एक ही औपनिवेशिक राज्य थे। अतः बंगाल नवजागरण का सीधा प्रभाव अन्य राज्यों की तुलना में पहले ओड़िशा पर ही पड़ा। बंगाल ब्रह्मसमाज की एक शाखा ‘उत्कालिय ब्रह्मसमाज’ के नाम से ‘बालेश्वर' में स्थापित हुई। जिसके माध्यम से पाश्चात्य शिक्षित उत्कलिय अपनी देश,जाति, धर्म, संस्कृति के उत्तरोत्तर उन्नति का विकास कार्य करने लगे। आगे चल कर ओड़िया भाषा अँग्रेज़ों व बंगाल के कुचक्रान्त की शिकार बनी। उनके द्वारा ओड़िया को बंगला से विकसित प्रमाणित कर मुलोत्पाटन करने की पुरज़ोर कोशिश हुई। इस कुत्सित चक्रान्त की परिणति यह हुई कि सरकार द्वारा 'ओड़िया भाषा द्वारा शिक्षादान' प्रत्याहार का आदेश पारित कर दिया गया।  इसके विरोध में ओड़िशा के शिक्षित वर्गों ने भी क्षुब्ध होकर आंदोलन छेड़ दिया। इस आंदोलन के पुरोधा बने उत्कल के वरपुत्र फ़क़ीर मोहन सेनापति। अंततः सरकार को भी सन्‌ 1870 में अपना आदेश प्रत्याहार करने के लिए बाध्य होना पड़ा    619ओड़िशा में ओड़िया भाषा को समाप्त करने का आदेश किस वर्ष वापस लिया गया?622

Comprehension:दिए गए गद्यांश को पढ़कर नीचे लिखे प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए ।भारत का संविधान भारतीय गणराज्य का सर्वोच्च कानून है। यह देश की राजनीतिक व्यवस्था के लिए रूपरेखा तैयार करता है, सरकार की संस्थाओं की शक्तियों एवं उत्तरदायित्वों को परिभाषित करता है। संविधान के द्वारा मौलिक अधिकारों की रक्षा के साथ-साथ शासन के सिद्धांतों को भी रेखांकित किया जाता है। संविधान में देश के प्रशासन का मार्गदर्शन करने वाले नियमों और विनियमों का एक समूह होता है। भारतीय संविधान राष्ट्र के लोकतांत्रिक आदर्शों और  आकांक्षाओं का प्रमाण है। इसका निर्माण सावधानीपूर्वक किया गया है, जो ऐतिहासिक संघर्षों और दूरदर्शी सिद्धांतों पर आधारित है, और यह भारत को एक अधिक न्यायपूर्ण, समावेशी और समृद्ध समाज की ओर ले जाने का मार्गदर्शन प्रदान करता है। भारतीय संविधान अपने मूल्यों को बनाए रखने, विविधता के बीच एकता को बढ़ावा देने और प्रत्येक नागरिक के अधिकारों और स्वतंत्रताओं की रक्षा करने के लिए महत्त्वपूर्ण है, इस प्रकार यह आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए एक उज्ज्वल भविष्य सुनिश्चित करता है।‘’भारत का संविधान भारतीय गणराज्य का सर्वोच्च कानून है।‘’

Comprehension:गद्यांश के आधार पर निम्नलिखित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।हमारे भारत का हर त्यौहार और उत्सव सिर्फ मौज-मस्ती नहीं, अपितु सांस्कृतिक, सामाजिक और वैज्ञानिक आधारों की कसौटी पर खरा उतरता है। हम खेतीहर संस्कृति वाले भारतवासी आज भी विजयदशमी पर नए जौ के अंकुर अपने मस्तक पर धारण करते हैं और उसे जय का प्रतीक मानते हैं। आने वाली नई फसल के अंकुर से हम अपनी विजय यात्रा का आरंभ करते हैं। विजयदशमी के दिन लोग नीलकंठ पक्षी के दर्शन करना चाहते हैं, इससे हम विषपायी शिव का दर्शन करते हैं। आदमी जब विजय के लिए निकलता है तो उसे अपयश, असफलता, संघर्ष और लोकनिंदा का गरल पीकर ही अपने को विजय लक्ष्य तक पहुंचना होता है।दीपावली पर अमावस की रात सबसे गहरी होती है। पावस के चार महीनों का सारा तमस असंख्य कीट-पतंग बनकर छोटे-छोटे दीयों के प्रकाश में जल जाता है। यह प्रतीक है कि आत्मा के तेज और सात्विकता में जलकर तमस का विनाश अवश्य होगा। पूर्वी भारत में यह कालीपूजा के रूप में मनाया जाता है। काली मोह और मद को जड़ से नाश करने वाली शक्ति है। इसी दिन व्यापारी नए-नए बहीखाते पूजते हैं। दिए अपनी रोशनी से बताते हैं कि अंधकार का कोई आधार नहीं होता यदि है तो प्रकाश उसे दूर करने का आह्वान करता है।विजयदशमी पर धारण किया जाने वाला अंकुरित जौ किसका प्रतीक होता है ?
